events.title: The English capture David II of Scotland at Neville's Cross
events.description: An English force defeated a Scottish invasion at Neville's Cross near Durham and captured King David II. He spent eleven years as a prisoner before being ransomed.
events.html: An English force defeated a Scottish invasion at Neville's Cross near Durham and captured King David II. He spent eleven years as a prisoner before being ransomed.

events.title: Burgoyne surrenders his army at Saratoga
events.description: British General John Burgoyne surrendered nearly 6,000 men to American forces at Saratoga, New York. The victory persuaded France to ally with the United States, a turning point in the Revolutionary War.
events.html: British General John Burgoyne surrendered nearly 6,000 men to American forces at Saratoga, New York. The victory persuaded France to ally with the United States, a turning point in the Revolutionary War.

events.title: Edison files his first motion picture caveat
events.description: Thomas Edison filed a patent caveat describing an 'optical phonograph' to record and reproduce moving images. The idea, developed largely by his assistant William Dickson, became the Kinetoscope.
events.html: Thomas Edison filed a patent caveat describing an 'optical phonograph' to record and reproduce moving images. The idea, developed largely by his assistant William Dickson, became the Kinetoscope.

events.title: The Queen opens Calder Hall nuclear power station
events.description: Elizabeth II opened Calder Hall in Cumberland, the world's first nuclear power station to supply electricity to a national grid on a commercial scale. It also produced plutonium for Britain's weapons programme.
events.html: Elizabeth II opened Calder Hall in Cumberland, the world's first nuclear power station to supply electricity to a national grid on a commercial scale. It also produced plutonium for Britain's weapons programme.

events.title: Mother Teresa is named winner of the Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced its Peace Prize for Mother Teresa, founder of the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, for her work among the poorest and dying.
